stemMd: Working alone, pump A empties a full tank in $12$ hours and pump B empties the same full tank in $18$ hours. Starting with the tank full, both pumps run together for $4$ hours, after which pump A is switched off and pump B continues alone. How many additional hours does pump B need to finish emptying the tank?
explanationMd:
Work with rates measured in tanks per hour, and take the full tank as $1$ unit of work.

$$\text{rate}_A = \frac{1}{12}, \qquad \text{rate}_B = \frac{1}{18}, \qquad \text{rate}_{A+B} = \frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{18} = \frac{3}{36} + \frac{2}{36} = \frac{5}{36}.$$

In the first $4$ hours together they empty

$$4 \times \frac{5}{36} = \frac{20}{36} = \frac{5}{9} \text{ of the tank},$$

so the fraction still to be emptied is $1 - \frac{5}{9} = \frac{4}{9}$.

Pump B alone works at $\frac{1}{18}$ of a tank per hour, so the time it needs is

$$t = \frac{4/9}{1/18} = \frac{4}{9} \times 18 = 8 \text{ hours}.$$

Check the answer by adding up the work done: A runs $4$ hours and does $\frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}$; B runs $4 + 8 = 12$ hours and does $\frac{12}{18} = \frac{2}{3}$; together $\frac{1}{3} + \frac{2}{3} = 1$, one whole tank. That total-work check is the fastest way to confirm any combined-rate answer.

distractorRationale.b: This assumes the two pumps emptied exactly half the tank in the first $4$ hours and so halves B's solo time of $18$ hours. They actually emptied $\frac{5}{9}$, slightly more than half, and the remaining work must be divided by B's rate rather than estimated.
distractorRationale.c: This counts only pump A's output during the first $4$ hours: $\frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}$ done, leaving $\frac{2}{3}$, so B would need $\frac{2}{3} \times 18 = 12$ hours. Pump B was also running during those first four hours.
distractorRationale.d: This counts only pump B's own output during the first $4$ hours: $\frac{4}{18} = \frac{2}{9}$ done, leaving $\frac{7}{9}$, so B would need $\frac{7}{9} \times 18 = 14$ hours. It ignores the work pump A contributed before being switched off.
distractorRationale.e: This is the time pump B needs to empty a full tank on its own. More than half the tank is already gone when pump A stops, so B cannot need its full solo time.

accessibilityText: Pump A empties a full tank in 12 hours and pump B empties it in 18 hours. Both run together for 4 hours, then pump A stops and pump B continues alone. Find how many more hours pump B needs to finish emptying the tank.

provenance.notes: Original item. Each distractor corresponds to omitting one pump's contribution or to an estimation shortcut; all five values are distinct integers.

review.author: gmat-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: Combined rate 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 per hour; in 4 hours they empty 20/36 = 5/9, leaving 4/9. B alone at 1/18 per hour needs (4/9)/(1/18) = 8 additional hours.

review.notes: Author verified via the total-work check that A's 4 hours plus B's 12 hours sum to exactly one tank. Awaiting blind independent solve.
